purpose: Learnable, executable ground truth for an AI Agent and human users. Read learning_guide and preprocessing_plan before repair_records.

learning_guide.how_to_use: JSON teaches an AI Agent what each problem means, how to detect it, and how to repair it. The notebook is the human-friendly problem/solution workbook. Python is the executable reference answer that reproduces the clean database.
learning_guide.important: Candidate detection and exact supervised verification are separate. When raw corruption destroyed information, exact recovery is explicitly labeled as oracle repair.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Insert zero-width Unicode characters into city names.

detection.guidance: Normalize Unicode and scan for zero-width/control characters that are invisible in ordinary previews.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT OrderID, ShipCity, hex(ShipCity) AS utf8_hex FROM Orders WHERE instr(ShipCity, char(8203)) > 0 OR instr(ShipCity, char(65279)) > 0

preprocessing.algorithm: NFKC-normalize text and remove zero-width/BOM characters.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: The function derives clean values from raw values and asserts equality with labels.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Insert invisible characters into quantity/unit descriptions.

detection.guidance: Normalize Unicode and scan for zero-width/control characters that are invisible in ordinary previews.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT ProductID, QuantityPerUnit, hex(QuantityPerUnit) AS utf8_hex FROM Products WHERE instr(QuantityPerUnit, char(8203)) > 0 OR instr(QuantityPerUnit, char(65279)) > 0

preprocessing.algorithm: NFKC-normalize text and remove zero-width/BOM characters.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: The function derives clean values from raw values and asserts equality with labels.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Clone customers under different IDs so key-based deduplication is insufficient.

detection.guidance: Group by business identity columns excluding the technical primary key; review the duplicate groups before deleting.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT duplicate.CustomerID, duplicate.CompanyName, duplicate.ContactName FROM Customers AS duplicate WHERE duplicate.CustomerID GLOB 'X[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customers AS original WHERE original.CustomerID != duplicate.CustomerID AND original.CompanyName = duplicate.CompanyName)

preprocessing.algorithm: Resolve business-identity duplicates and delete only injected clones.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: The function derives clean values from raw values and asserts equality with labels.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Create subtle adjacent-character typos in shipping entity names.

detection.guidance: Normalize text then compare edit distance/token similarity against canonical entity names.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.ShipName, c.CompanyName AS customer_name FROM Orders AS o LEFT JOIN Customers AS c ON c.CustomerID=o.CustomerID WHERE o.ShipName IS NOT NULL AND c.CompanyName IS NOT NULL AND o.ShipName != c.CompanyName

preprocessing.algorithm: Fuzzy matching generates candidates; the supervised label selects the exact canonical entity name.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Move internally coherent address blocks to the wrong order entities.

detection.guidance: The address block is internally valid; compare its ownership against customer ID and ship name.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.ShipAddress, o.ShipCity, o.ShipPostalCode, o.ShipCountry, c.Address AS customer_address, c.City AS customer_city, c.PostalCode AS customer_postal, c.Country AS customer_country FROM Orders AS o LEFT JOIN Customers AS c ON c.CustomerID=o.CustomerID WHERE c.CustomerID IS NULL OR o.ShipAddress IS NOT c.Address OR o.ShipCity IS NOT c.City OR o.ShipPostalCode IS NOT c.PostalCode OR o.ShipCountry IS NOT c.Country

preprocessing.algorithm: The block is internally valid but belongs to another entity; restore four supervised fields together.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Mix explicit orphan entities into a dataset dominated by subtler errors.

detection.guidance: Use PRAGMA foreign_key_check and NOT EXISTS anti-joins from child keys to parent keys.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT o.OrderID, o.CustomerID FROM Orders AS o LEFT JOIN Customers AS c ON c.CustomerID=o.CustomerID WHERE o.CustomerID IS NOT NULL AND c.CustomerID IS NULL

preprocessing.algorithm: Anti-join detects GHOST, but exact original ownership requires the supervised relationship.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Assign products to different existing suppliers.

detection.guidance: A passing FK is insufficient: validate that the referenced entity is semantically correct for this record.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT ProductID, ProductName, SupplierID FROM Products ORDER BY ProductID

preprocessing.algorithm: The FK is valid and only semantic reference knowledge identifies the correct supplier.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Assign products to different existing categories.

detection.guidance: A passing FK is insufficient: validate that the referenced entity is semantically correct for this record.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT p.ProductID, p.ProductName, p.CategoryID, c.CategoryName FROM Products AS p LEFT JOIN Categories AS c ON c.CategoryID=p.CategoryID ORDER BY p.ProductID

preprocessing.algorithm: The FK is valid and only semantic product knowledge identifies the correct category.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Reassign orders to other valid customers while retaining original shipping identities.

detection.guidance: Compare foreign-key identity with denormalized names, addresses, geography and historical assignment patterns.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT o.OrderID, o.CustomerID, o.ShipName, o.ShipAddress, c.CompanyName, c.Address FROM Orders AS o LEFT JOIN Customers AS c ON c.CustomerID=o.CustomerID WHERE c.CustomerID IS NULL OR o.ShipName IS NOT c.CompanyName OR o.ShipAddress IS NOT c.Address

preprocessing.algorithm: Cross-field identity evidence detects drift; exact ownership is restored from labels.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Rotate valid employee identifiers among orders.

detection.guidance: Compare foreign-key identity with denormalized names, addresses, geography and historical assignment patterns.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT OrderID, EmployeeID, OrderDate, ShipCountry FROM Orders ORDER BY OrderID

preprocessing.algorithm: All IDs are valid and distributionally plausible; exact assignment requires oracle labels.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Rotate valid shipper IDs without creating a foreign-key violation.

detection.guidance: Compare foreign-key identity with denormalized names, addresses, geography and historical assignment patterns.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT o.OrderID, o.ShipVia, s.CompanyName AS shipper, o.ShipCountry FROM Orders AS o LEFT JOIN Shippers AS s ON s.ShipperID=o.ShipVia ORDER BY o.OrderID

preprocessing.algorithm: All shipper IDs are valid; exact historical assignment requires oracle labels.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Shift valid ISO order timestamps one year while leaving related dates unchanged.

detection.guidance: Check timestamps against sibling dates, accepted date range and temporal distribution shifts.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, RequiredDate, ShippedDate FROM Orders WHERE datetime(OrderDate) > datetime(RequiredDate) OR datetime(OrderDate) > datetime(ShippedDate)

preprocessing.algorithm: Reverse the generator's exact +365-day shift and preserve the baseline date/time precision.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: The function derives clean values from raw values and asserts equality with labels.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Apply a silent 100x unit-scale error to freight.

detection.guidance: Compare value ratios to peer/reference values and search for 10x/100x scale clusters.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT OrderID, Freight, ShipCountry FROM Orders WHERE Freight > 0 AND Freight < 6 ORDER BY Freight

preprocessing.algorithm: Reverse the injected 1/100 scale and round to the baseline precision.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: The function derives clean values from raw values and asserts equality with labels.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Rotate plausible prices among unrelated order lines, preserving type and global range.

detection.guidance: Join the row to its product/order/entity context; validate the value conditionally rather than only by global min/max.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT d.OrderID, d.ProductID, d.UnitPrice, p.UnitPrice AS current_product_price FROM "Order Details" AS d JOIN Products AS p ON p.ProductID=d.ProductID WHERE d.UnitPrice != p.UnitPrice

preprocessing.algorithm: Historical prices can legitimately differ from current product price; exact line price requires labels.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Permute valid quantities across unrelated order lines.

detection.guidance: Join the row to its product/order/entity context; validate the value conditionally rather than only by global min/max.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT ProductID, COUNT(*) AS lines, AVG(Quantity) AS mean_quantity, MIN(Quantity) AS min_quantity, MAX(Quantity) AS max_quantity FROM "Order Details" GROUP BY ProductID ORDER BY ProductID

preprocessing.algorithm: Permuted quantities preserve valid range and distribution; exact row values require labels.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Reassign valid discount levels so univariate profiling remains plausible.

detection.guidance: Join the row to its product/order/entity context; validate the value conditionally rather than only by global min/max.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT OrderID, ProductID, Discount, Quantity, UnitPrice FROM "Order Details" WHERE Discount > 0 ORDER BY OrderID, ProductID

preprocessing.algorithm: Every discount remains valid; exact contextual discount requires supervised labels.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Move plausible contact identities and roles between customer entities.

detection.guidance: Validate the group of identity fields together; individually plausible values can belong to different entities.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT CustomerID, CompanyName, ContactName, ContactTitle FROM Customers ORDER BY CustomerID

preprocessing.algorithm: Plausible contact pairs were moved between entities; exact identity requires labels.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.

preprocessing_plan.problem: Rotate valid product prices while preserving the aggregate distribution.

detection.guidance: Join the row to its product/order/entity context; validate the value conditionally rather than only by global min/max.
detection.candidate_sql: SELECT p.ProductID, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice, AVG(d.UnitPrice) AS historical_mean FROM Products AS p LEFT JOIN "Order Details" AS d ON d.ProductID=p.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID ORDER BY p.ProductID

preprocessing.algorithm: Prices were permuted while preserving distribution; exact product price requires labels.
preprocessing.oracle_usage: Uses clean_value labels because raw data cannot uniquely recover the original.
